archiveTitle: Daily Brief | The Binding of Isaac removes undisclosed AI music

entries.headline: The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ removes undisclosed AI music after a review backlash
entries.summary: PC Gamer reports that Repentance+ added music without an AI disclosure to its GTA-style Crime Mode daily challenge. Recent Steam reviews briefly fell to 8% positive, and the disputed music was removed after the backlash.
entries.verification: The full PC Gamer report was reviewed. This item uses only its account of the update, the Steam review snapshot at the time and the music's removal; it does not treat the changing review score as final or infer an undisclosed production process.
entries.timeNote: PC Gamer published the report at 9:11 AM Beijing time on November 23, within the fixed window. The 8% figure is a snapshot of recent Steam reviews at the time of reporting.

entries.headline: The original Metal Gear Solid can hand control of the M1 tank to a second controller
entries.summary: AUTOMATON reports that researchers found a way to control the M1 tank boss in the original 1998 Metal Gear Solid with a second controller on a second playthrough. Triggering it requires 14 input sequences at 30-frame intervals, and the demonstration used a macro.
entries.verification: The full AUTOMATON report was reviewed. The item follows its description of the demonstration, second-playthrough condition and macro-assisted input limits, without presenting the discovery as an official two-player mode.
entries.timeNote: AUTOMATON published the report at 1:28 PM Beijing time on November 22, within the fixed window.

entries.headline: Guild Exploration Team reconstructs 78 adventurers' relationships from 1,000 days of records
entries.summary: An AUTOMATON feature examines this document-deduction game, in which players use 1,000 days of guild records to reconstruct the teams, fates and relationships of 78 adventurers across 20 parties. The article argues that the characters' unstated emotions and experiences are as important as organizing the evidence.
entries.verification: The full AUTOMATON feature was reviewed. Its numbers, gameplay description and analysis of the characters' relationships are kept within the article's explicit scope.
entries.timeNote: AUTOMATON published the feature at 3:09 PM Beijing time on November 22, within the fixed window.

entries.headline: Grand Theft Auto VI developer honors his late mother with an in-game memorial
entries.summary: IGN reports that Rockstar QA developer Matt Green described how his mother influenced his path into game development. She died eight months before the game's release, and the team later added her name to a memorial wall in Leonida.
entries.verification: The full IGN report was reviewed. The factual chain is limited to the developer's public account of his mother and the in-game memorial wall, without extending the claim to other memorials.
entries.timeNote: IGN published the report at 7:23 AM Beijing time on November 23, within the fixed window.

entries.headline: Rockstar explains why darts and bowling were cut from Grand Theft Auto VI
entries.summary: Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson told VGC that the team did not have unlimited time or budget, and interactions that failed to meet its internal quality bar were left out. Darts and bowling therefore did not make it into Grand Theft Auto VI.
entries.verification: IGN's full relay of the VGC interview was reviewed. This item uses only Rob Nelson's identifiable comments about resource and quality trade-offs and does not frame the relay as a separate Rockstar announcement.
entries.timeNote: IGN published the report at 4:37 AM Beijing time on November 23, within the fixed window; its source chain points to a VGC interview.

entries.headline: Yoshinori Kitase discusses how the Final Fantasy VII remake series reimagines the original
entries.summary: 4Gamer reports that original director and remake-series producer Yoshinori Kitase delivered a G-STAR 2026 talk in South Korea on how Final Fantasy VII has been rebuilt for a new era.
entries.verification: The fixed 4Gamer page snapshot in the packet was reviewed. This item states only the speaker's role, the event and the announced subject of the talk, without adding design details absent from the snapshot.
entries.timeNote: 4Gamer published the report at 11:46 AM Beijing time on November 22, within the fixed window.

entries.headline: HITORIASOBI blends deckbuilding with a 3D board and reveals its obscured title on a second run
entries.summary: 4Gamer played HITORIASOBI at WePlay 2026. The game has Rinachi command toy soldiers on a board, combining roguelike deckbuilding with a 3D tabletop. A developer interview also says a second playthrough reveals the title's hidden word and the darker reason behind the story.
entries.verification: The fixed 4Gamer page snapshot in the packet was reviewed. The gameplay, second-playthrough structure and interview claims all remain within that hands-on report.
entries.timeNote: 4Gamer published the report at 11:00 AM Beijing time on November 22, within the fixed window.

entries.headline: Concerto on the White Keys: Bass Hero turns a stripped keyboard and four pens into a bass controller
entries.summary: 4Gamer played C11 Games' new title at WePlay Expo 2026. The booth controller removed several keycaps and laid four ballpoint pens across the keyboard as strings, letting players hold and operate it in a bass-like position.
entries.verification: The fixed 4Gamer show-floor report was reviewed. The controller construction, developer and event identity follow the page's description, without inferring a production version.
entries.timeNote: 4Gamer published the report at 9:30 AM Beijing time on November 23, within the fixed window.

entries.headline: NVIDIA hotfix 621.35 reportedly fails to stop continued driver log writes to SSDs
entries.summary: PC Gamer reports that some users found recent NVIDIA drivers continually overwriting log files, with one extreme report reaching roughly 30 GB per hour. Users continued to report writes after hotfix 621.35, leading the article to recommend temporarily rolling back to 621.01.
entries.verification: The full PC Gamer report was reviewed. The hotfix's failure is explicitly limited to user reports summarized by the outlet, and the 30 GB-per-hour figure remains an extreme case rather than a universal result.
entries.timeNote: PC Gamer published the report at 6:31 AM Beijing time on November 23, within the fixed window.
